subject: Post-call: air-gapped hosting eligibility & decision path
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@medsafe.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Sep 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: air-gapped hosting eligibility & decision path

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery so the team is aligned and we have concrete next steps. Please correct anything I misstate.

Summary of pain / drivers you shared:
- Regulatory auditor requires physical isolation for any model hosting that touches PHI-derived identifiers; encryption-in-use is not sufficient for this workload.
- Customer control over keys + full audit trail is mandatory (KMS/HSM + retention policy).
- Strict network egress policy: no outbound internet from the inference tier except to a monitored proxy host.
- Large batch inference for nightly scoring (3–4M tokens/day) + low-latency interactive queries for clinicians (p95 <300ms).

Goals you described:
1) Run inference in an air-gapped on-prem site (or VPC with enforced egress block) within Q4.
2) Preserve model update cadence (weekly minor updates, monthly major) while ensuring reproducible rollout and rollback.
3) Maintain Redwood console telemetry in a way that satisfies the audit team (we discussed an agent that ships masked telemetry to your SIEM).

Technical constraints we identified
- Network: no public IPs for inference nodes; NAT only via a central proxy in your DMZ.
- Storage: customer-managed object storage with encryption keys only you control.
- Hardware: prefer 2x A100-equivalent nodes for initial capacity; ability to expand for nightly batch runs.
- Air-gap: occasional cross-site transfers for model artifacts via signed media or secure import bucket (we discussed rsync + signed package validation).

Actions / owners / timings
- Elena / MedSafe: share the initial network diagram and current firewall rules (we referenced an existing diagram in the call). Deliver by Thu 2027-09-23. [Attachment: initial_network_sketch.png optional]
- Rishi (redwood): draft an on-prem deployment architecture with the egress-control pattern and model import workflow. Deliver by Mon 2027-09-27.
- Priyom (redwood): prepare a compliance-ready runbook explaining telemetry masking, keyflow, and audit logs to show to MedSafe auditors. Deliver by Tue 2027-09-28.
- Ava: coordinate a follow-up technical review with your infra and security leads (30–45m). Target week of 2027-09-27.

Open questions we flagged (please prioritize which matter most to you)
1) Can your proxy support mTLS for permitted outbound connections (we need to know whether Redwood can rely on an authenticated proxy or whether model import must be pushed via removable media)?
2) Are nightly batch workloads allowed to run with temporary elevated egress for model fetch (short window), or must all artifact delivery be strictly offline?
3) Any constraint on HSM vendor / KMIP support?

Attachments I’m including: initial_network_sketch.png (from your architecture doc you referenced), medsafe_hosting_requirements.xlsx (your questionnaire export we transcribed), SOC2-excerpt.pdf (example audit excerpt for telemetry minimal set).

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule the tech review and Rishi will draft the architecture doc.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

[Attachment: medsafe_hosting_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: initial_network_sketch.png (image)]
From: Elena Torres <elena@medsafe.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, MedSafe Security Team <security@medsafe.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped hosting eligibility & decision path

Ava —

This is great, thank you for the crisp summary. A few clarifications:
- We cannot allow any short-lived egress windows for model fetches; all model artifacts must be delivered using signed media or staged into an internal import bucket that is only accessible from the on-prem network via a controlled jump host.
- The proxy supports mTLS but only for upstream targets we pre-authorize; we would prefer the push/import model to reduce operational approval overhead.
- HSM: we use Thales/Entrust currently and require KMIP compatibility.

We’ll share the up-to-date firewall matrix and an updated diagram by end of day Thu 2027-09-23. I’ll loop in our infra lead separately for the tech review.

—Elena
Elena Torres
VP, IT & Security | MedSafe
elena@medsafe.ai

[Attachment: medsafe_network_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@medsafe.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped hosting eligibility & decision path

Thanks Elena — that helps a lot. Technical notes / clarifying questions from my side: 

1) Import workflow idea: signed artifact + checksum verification + offline validation node. We’ll propose a carrier/transfer checklist that mirrors your auditor requirements.

2) On the runtime side, we’ll plan for no outbound DNS and no direct internet routes from the inference subnet. Redwood’s agent will be configured to:  a) buffer masked telemetry locally and b) surface audit logs via an export tool you run to your SIEM. That keeps Redwood from needing outbound connections.

3) Capacity: for the batch profile you described we recommend starting with 2x40GB GPUs (or equivalent) and a small GPU pool for interactive queries. We’ll include back-of-envelope cost/latency numbers in the architecture doc.

4) HSM/KMIP: we can integrate with customer HSMs; need to confirm KMIP endpoints and cert rotation policy.

Next steps: I’ll draft the architecture and include two deployment variants (on-prem air-gap with importer; VPC-sequestered w/ enforced egress via proxy). Expect the doc by Mon 2027-09-27. Priyom will draft the compliance runbook.

-Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

[Inline: quoted earlier bullet from Ava about model update cadence]
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@medsafe.ai>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: air-gapped hosting eligibility & decision path

Elena / team —

Appreciate the quick turn on clarifications. I’ll focus the runbook on three artifacts: (1) telemetry masking & local buffer policy, (2) importer validation checklist, (3) audit log shipping playbook.

Can you confirm the auditor’s retention window requirement for logs (we’ll propose sensible defaults but want to match your policy)? Also: do you require signed attestations for every model update, or only for major releases?

If you’re good, I’ll schedule a 45m technical review for Tue 2027-09-28 09:00 PT (proposed). Please reply with availability and I’ll send calendar invite + dial-in.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com
